body: I may want to help on this. `--fix` has done funny things to my indentation. Hoping this is related.
Just as I was reading this someone starts fixing this. Really cool!

I'm not sure if it's the same thing, but I found this issue with `--fix`:

``` sh
eslint file.js --rule "indent: [error, tab]" --fix
```

**Input:**

``` js
if(true) {
    foo(); // tab
  bar(); // 2 spaces
}
```

**Output**

``` js
if(true) {
    foo(); // tab
                                        bar(); // 2 spaces, 10 tabs
}
```

**Expected output**

``` js
if(true) {
    foo(); // tab
    bar(); // tab
}
```
I can confirm with @bfred-it that attempt to convert indent from spaces to tabs mess up all of the files.

issue.body:
**What version of ESLint are you using?**
ESlint 3.4.0

**What parser (default, Babel-ESLint, etc.) are you using?**
**Please show your full configuration:**
`/*eslint indent: ["warn", "tab"]*/`

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue.**
Consider this simple  code:

```
/*eslint indent: ["warn", "tab"]*/
    var a = 1;
alert(a);
```

**What did you expect to happen?**
Unless there's a special option in the `indent` rule to configure otherwise,
all lines should be expected to have at least no indentation (=0 tabs),
so ESLint should show warning for line 2 (`Expected indentation of 0 tab character but found 1`) 
not 3.

**What actually happened? Please include the actual, raw output from ESLint.**
Because the 1st code line has 1 tab indentation, 
all code lines are expected to have at least 1 tab indentation,
so ESLint shows:

```
  3:1  warning  Expected indentation of 1 tab character but found 0       indent

✖ 1 problem (0 errors, 1 warning)
```

issue.body:
Opening this issue to give us a place to discuss how we would like to move forward with the `indent` rule, given the number of open issues we have and the complexity of the rule. I'm leaving all the currently open `indent` issues open (even if they have reached the time we've agreed upon to close old issues) so we can take stock, but am not opposed to closing them after we discuss. Might even be worth creating a GitHub Project or milestone to track this when we've decided how we want to proceed.
